chunks: 2067 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a guest from among his brethren staying with him, and the Day of al-Fiṭr arrives: should he pay the fiṭrah on his behalf?
He عليه السلام said: “Yes. Al-fiṭrah is obligatory for everyone whom he supports, whether male or female, young or old, free or enslaved.”

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةَ: zakat al-fiṭrah, the charity due at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٍ: an enslaved person under one’s authority and maintenance
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْفِطْرِ: the day of Eid al-Fiṭr when fiṭrah becomes due

ai.seo_question: Is zakat al-fiṭrah obligatory for a guest staying in one’s home on Eid al-Fiṭr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on zakat al-fiṭrah at the end of Ramadan. It states that fiṭrah is obligatory on behalf of all dependents maintained by a person, including a guest under his support on the Day of al-Fiṭr. The narration highlights the broad scope of financial responsibility in this act of worship.
